claims.text: Residual internal and substrate-induced stresses primarily govern the low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanostructures.
Residual stresses disrupt a uniform magnetostructural phase transition in these nanostructures.
Post-deposition thermal annealing can relieve the residual stresses.
Stress-relief annealing will enhance the magnetocaloric effect relative to the as-deposited state.
Stress-relief annealing will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the as-deposited state.
The as-deposited nanostructures have significant internal strain and substrate-induced stress.
The as-deposited nanostructures contain stress-associated microstructural defects.
A suitable annealing treatment can relieve stress without significantly changing alloy composition or nanostructure.
Interface defects and grain-boundary disorder arise from the nanoscale deposition process.
Residual stresses pin magnetic domain walls.
Residual stresses disrupt the magnetoelastic coupling required for a complete and uniform magnetostructural phase transformation.
Annealing-induced stress relaxation facilitates a more coherent magnetostructural phase transition.
A more coherent phase transition increases the associated latent-heat exchange.
Increased latent-heat exchange enhances the magnetocaloric response.
A more coherent phase transition reduces hysteresis.
The as-deposited state has a diminished magnetocaloric effect because of high residual stresses and microstructural defects.
The as-deposited state has significant hysteresis because of high residual stresses and microstructural defects.
The proposed behavior applies under low applied fields near the phase-transformation temperature.
The magnitude of the response depends on annealing conditions and nanoscale structure.
